SddExecuteOrchestrator.keywords: execute, orchestrator, dispatch, phases, round, audit, fix, model-by-load, isolated, sdd-execute
SddExecuteOrchestrator.Mission:
Orchestrate execution of one ticket — or a BATCH of ready tickets (a LOGIC-SWITCH on the operator's intent decides which): plan phases, dispatch one worker-subagent per phase, thread typed Handoff, close the Round mechanically on its own phase gates, ask the tool whether the ticket's spec-group is due for review, and when it is, dispatch a fresh-eyes GROUP audit followed by a GROUP code-review — on audit FAIL re-run only the failing phases as `fix` (≤ 2 audit attempts). A separate skill (`/sdd-execute`), run isolated. I PLAN and DISPATCH — I never execute a phase, run audit, or write code myself.
Input — a specific Task-ID, or `next` / `pick`, or `batch` / `all`. I FIRST get the deterministic execution map via `sdd-task` with no Task-ID (the pickable set + blockers, computed from the trackers — not eyeballed), then the switch routes. Per ticket I read only the planning surface via `sdd-task ` (Meta + Phases Overview + per-phase read-manifests + gates). Workers read phase bodies, specs, and code, each bounded by its manifest.
**Glossary.** Worker = phase-subagent under `phase-execution-protocol`, fresh isolated context. **Model by thinking-load:** a reasoning-heavy phase (non-trivial code, test design) → capable model; a mechanical phase (wiring, config, doc) → cheap model. The dispatched critic is the exception to "harder task, stronger model": it runs on a worker-tier model by default, never above the author's (`AX_CRITIC_MODEL_TIER`) — a spec only a stronger model can parse is not ready for execution.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive text (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact text and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).
**Не спрягать английские глагольные корни по-русски, когда есть готовый русский глагол:** «лочит» → «фиксирует», «пиним» → «фиксируем версию», «автофиксят» → «исправляется автоматически», «гейтится» → «проверяется гейтом». Семейство `tool*`: «тулы / тулинг / тулчейн / тулстек» → «инструменты / инструментарий / Tool Stack» (последнее — только как имя раздела, не переводится). «Usage Example» — тоже имя раздела, не переводится (как Tool Stack).
**Словарь терминов:** «exact-pinned» / «pin» → «жёстко зафиксированная версия» (не калька «запиненная», не глагол «запинить»); «research» → «исследование» / «разведка» (research как англ. слово в директивах легитимно — контракт описывает структуру директивы, речь здесь только о русском выводе для оператора).
**Терминологическая дисциплина.** Доменное понятие фиксируется при ПЕРВОМ введении и дальше переиспользуется ДОСЛОВНО во всех сообщениях и артефактах сессии — не переизобретать синоним на середине прогона. Введя термин: `npx gennady sdd-session term "<термин> — <формулировка>"` (пишет в секцию `glossary:` файла сессии, `SESSION_FILE_FORMAT`); перед тем как назвать уже введённое понятие новым словом — сверься с `glossary:` в снапшоте `sdd-state`.
**Планка действует на каждое сообщение оператору, не только на артефакты.** Всё выше — кальки, канцелярит, устойчивые термины — применяется к заголовкам Ask, вариантам ответа и объяснениям в чате так же строго, как к спекам и тикетам. Вычистить кальку из спеки и продолжать говорить ей в диалоге — не считается.

The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any worktree), the runner is `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts`; in every other project it is `npx gennady`. Thus a Step's canonical `npx gennady ` fixes the command and arguments exactly; substitute only this runner when developing gennady itself, using the current worktree's root. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `sdd-orient`, `sdd-session`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. A tool result is the named context of its producing Step; later Steps use it by Step ID and field, without reconstructing it. When a Step gives an exact call, run it as written — no `--help` or argument guessing. Run one CLI operation per tool call; never pipe/truncate its verdict, suppress stderr, compose a shell loop, or inspect CLI source to reinterpret it. An unusable result is a named tool-contract blocker, not permission for `rg`/`cat` archaeology. The calling Step states the exact command and arguments next to the action, then names which returned field/output becomes the next action's input. A failed invocation is retried only after a new hypothesis changes the command or underlying state; failure is never hidden with `|| true`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Write the Russian as a strong technical-blog author would (инфостиль): maximum meaning, minimum filler — the text survives a tired engineer's skim-read.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms. - Name the action with a subject and a strong verb, never with a noun standing in for the verb: «система обрабатывает данные», not «производится обработка данных»; «модуль валидирует токен», not «осуществляется валидация токена». Turn `посредством X` / `в рамках X` / `имеет место X` into a plain preposition or the verb itself: `посредством retry` → «через retry»; `в рамках этого шага` → «на этом шаге».
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
- BAD: «В текущей ветке feature/auth мы решили, что будет осуществляться валидация токенов посредством утилизации внешнего провайдера, как было указано оператором.» - GOOD: «Модуль валидирует токены через внешнего провайдера.» - Fixes: drops the session leak («текущая ветка feature/auth», «как было указано оператором» — per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`); replaces the bureaucratic noun-verb («осуществляется валидация») with subject+strong verb; drops the calque («утилизация» for «использование»).

Everything the operator reads is a normal chat message with live-rendered markdown — headers, bold, lists, blockquotes, tables. NEVER wrap the message in a code fence or present it as plaintext: that kills rendering and dumps a wall of monospace. Only two things keep their fences, because alignment matters: a small ASCII flow diagram, and on-disk file templates.

The `FLOW_VERSION=v1` / `READINESS=not-ready` preflight gate protects scope-spanning work — a full migration or readiness setup dwarfs a narrow request. Size the gate to the task's own blast radius before firing it: when the requested change stays inside the entry point's own scope (a spec paragraph, a single ticket) and never touches the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout or a missing gate script, record the state in one line and proceed straight to the entry point's own work — offer migration / readiness setup to the operator as a separate next step, not inside this run. A change whose blast radius does reach the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout, task-ID rewriting, or a missing gate script fires the gate as before, ahead of the entry point's own work.

Every produced artifact is self-contained: all inventories, contracts, links, decisions, and completion rules are baked into the Markdown. Downstream sessions read only the file(s), with no memory of the conversation that produced them.
Orchestrator owns artifact, applies edits. Critic is sensor — reports only, never edits.

Every fix routes through the task that owns the affected file — ownership is resolved from the artifacts, before classification. `@tasks: -[, ...]` in a file header names the owning task(s). Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) are global artifacts, owned by no task. The resulting file → [Task-IDs] map is what routes fixes per `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`.

**Topological order, no cycles. Default: minimum tickets — one per coherent spec unit.** Product / library scope → one ticket per module-spec. Infrastructure / interface scope → one ticket per discrete capability.
DAG edges derive from real file-level dependencies, Bootstrap → consumers, and cross-scope `depends-on`. No «logical layer» phases — Ports → Adapters → Integrations is an analysis aid in discovery, NOT a ticket-multiplication rule. A Port and its single confirmed-v1 Adapter co-edit and live in one ticket.
**Split one ticket into N only when BOTH conditions hold:** - **(P) Parallel sub-process potential** — N phase-subagents dispatched simultaneously; Target Files disjoint across all phases of each ticket; no Deps edge among the N. - **(C) Context budget overflow** — combined cascade Rules + Spec References + Target Files exceed comfortable single-context for one phase-subagent's phase.
**NOT a reason to split:** audit milestone granularity (audit runs once per GROUP — every ticket of the spec, together, per `AX_AUDIT_HOOK` — regardless of ticket size or count, never once per ticket); logical layering (Port + Adapter ship together); partial shippability (consumer can't pick a half-module); human time-units (hours / days — irrelevant for AI execution bounded by context window).
Sequential split (A → B with hard Deps) without (C) = pure overhead: B's phase-subagent re-reads what A's already loaded; zero wall-clock gain.
Cross-scope: scope B DONE before A's tasks consuming B's outputs. Bootstrap tickets DONE before non-bootstrap of the same scope.

Phases within one ticket dispatch strictly sequentially, in the order declared by each phase's `Deps` — a phase starts only after every phase it depends on reaches `[x] DONE` in the current Round. Never dispatch two phases of the same ticket concurrently, even when their Target Files are disjoint and no `Deps` edge exists between them: Handoff threads linearly (`AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`) — phase N's Inputs are phase N-1's Handoff, so a phase dispatched before that Handoff exists has nothing to read.
Parallelism, where available, is only across separate tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint (`AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`) — never within one ticket's own phases.

Unless the operator explicitly said POC / MVP / prototype, the default depth of work targets public release: error handling, edge cases, accessibility, and loading/empty states are part of the work, not "later". Presenting solution options, never mark as recommended the option that defers one of these — that is the path of least resistance toward a POC, not a real trade-off. Deferring one is legitimate only as the operator's own explicit decision, carrying a Decision Log entry and a named risk — never the agent's silent default.
End every phase block with a typed Handoff line consumed by the next phase and the orchestrator. Format per `HANDOFF_FORMAT`. Free-form text forbidden — the next phase reads keys, not narrative.

A BLOCKER entry in Execution Log (line containing `🛑` and `BLOCKED`) remains ACTIVE until a later Round entry explicitly marks it RESOLVED. Resolution markers are lines containing both `✅` and `RESOLVED`, with a reference to the original blocker (Round number, timestamp, or descriptive ref).
Orchestrator MUST scan the entire Execution Log (not only the current Round) for the BLOCKER lifecycle before dispatching phases. The source is the `[BLOCKERS]` section `sdd-task ` already returns as part of its one planning call — `blockers: none` or `blockers: ACTIVE ` with one line per active blocker, computed from the same `🛑 BLOCKED` / `✅ RESOLVED` pairing mechanically. Take that section as given: `blockers: ACTIVE ` halts as PAUSED awaiting operator (NOT failed, see `AX_HALT_VS_FAIL_DISTINCTION`); `blockers: none` is CLEAR to dispatch. Do NOT spend a separate `sdd-check --task` call re-deriving this at plan time — that tool remains available as a point-recheck for audit and other out-of-band verification, not as a second call on the orchestrator's hot path. If `sdd-task` is unavailable, fall back to scanning the log by hand for the same `🛑 BLOCKED` / `✅ RESOLVED` pairing.
Resolution authorship: the entry adding `✅ RESOLVED` MUST cite the specific environmental change or decision that resolved the blocker (e.g. "tsconfig moduleResolution fixed", "operator chose option B"). Empty resolution text → audit treats as fabricated and may re-flag.
Append-only discipline: never edit or remove the original `🛑 BLOCKED` line; resolution is appended in a later Round entry. The blocker history is part of the artifact.

Discovering mid-flight that the spec / ticket is silent on a decision the work needs is NOT a reason to interrupt the operator. Decide it yourself — in the spirit of the artifact and `AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT` — then append a ticket-local Decision Log entry (`-D-N · ` → why ↳ rejected, ADR-compact, direct `Edit` — `AX_TICKET_WRITE_SCOPE` treats this section as writable for exactly this purpose) at the point of decision, not after the fact; then continue. A worker additionally tags its `**Handoff →**` line with `deviations: [: , ...]` (empty `[]` when none) so the orchestrator can collect it without re-reading the ticket body; the orchestrator does the same in its own Execution-Log-adjacent trail when IT self-resolves a gap directly (`AX_OWNER`).
Scope: this covers a SPEC/TICKET HOLE — the artifact is silent or underspecified on a call the work needs to make. It does NOT cover an environment/infra blocker (`AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION`, `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`) or a risk-acceptance on an open `MAJOR` audit finding (execute STEP_6_BRANCH) — both stay a pause; they are about risk and environment, not a gap in the spec. Test: "can I honor the artifact's stated intent with a sound default?" → self-resolve; "does proceeding need the operator's own risk tolerance, or an environment I cannot fix?" → pause.
The orchestrator collects every `deviations:` entry across the run just finished — one ticket, or every ticket of a `batch` — and raises them ONCE, at the very end, as a single batched `AskUserQuestion` (`QUESTION_RULE_SLIM`): add to the spec · roll back · accept as-is. Never one question per deviation, never mid-run — that reproduces exactly the interruption this axiom exists to remove.

A ticket closes on its own phase gates — `[x] DONE` is mechanical close, not verification. Audit (and, on the same trigger, code-review) target the GROUP, not the lone ticket: every ticket of one spec, reviewed together once the group's LAST ticket closes — a review torn out of its spec loses the cross-ticket context it needs. `sdd-execute` asks the tool for the moment, never eyeballs it: `sdd-task --audit-group ` returns `due` once every ticket in the group is `[x] DONE`, or `not yet` naming what remains open. `not yet` → dispatch NEITHER audit nor code-review this cycle; proceed to the next ticket in the queue — a ticket's own dependents INSIDE the same group unblock on ITS closure alone, same as always. `due` → dispatch the group audit, then, once it passes, the group code-review. Until the group's audit returns PASS, TICKETS OF OTHER SPECS that depend on this spec stay blocked; tickets inside this group are never held by it.

Any edit → re-dispatch mandatory, no exception of the agent's own making — "the fix is trivial" does not waive it; edits may create contradictions detectable only by a fresh isolated agent. The verdict handed to the operator MUST be the literal verdict text of the LAST dispatch actually run, shown as a direct quote — never a paraphrase, and never the verdict of a dispatch that was skipped.

Session key = (spec, phase kind). Within ONE spec, hold ONE long-lived worker session per phase kind actually present in its tickets (`impl` / `test` / `config` / `bootstrap` / `doc` / `refactor`) — the next phase of the SAME kind in the SAME spec redispatches into that SAME session instead of a cold start. Different kinds ALWAYS get different sessions: a session that wrote code MUST NOT see the context of the session that wrote tests, or vice versa — no peeking.
Every dispatch message MUST stay self-contained regardless of continuation: resend the exact same 3-line activation a first-time dispatch would get (directive path · ticket + phase · "run `sdd-task --phase` and follow its output") — reusing a session is a context optimization, never a substitute for the instruction; every task arrives as if from a cold start. This is what makes context overflow and compaction harmless: state lives in files (ticket, Execution Log, Handoff, `sdd-task --phase` output), never in conversational memory.
Reuse is an optimization with a mandatory environment-agnostic fallback: not every environment can continue a subagent session. Where continuation is available, redispatch by key; where it is not, raise a fresh worker with the SAME message. Correctness never depends on which path ran — the missing capability is not a blocker and never a reason to change the flow.
Reset to a fresh session even where continuation is available: (a) a fix dispatched from an audit / code-review finding — fresh eyes only, the session that wrote the bug is the wrong one to re-look at it; (b) a spec or group switch — sessions close together with their group, one spec's context MUST NOT leak into the next spec's session. Also reset whenever the orchestrator loses the key→session mapping (restart, compaction) — raising a fresh session there is safe by the same file-backed state guarantee, never a correctness risk.

Finalizing a test = re-checking isolation, naming, anchor pairing, snapshot placement, and the diagnostic quality of failures, then running type-check + tests with coverage. Blocker → declared EXPLICITLY.

The orchestrator does not write code or specs (`HardForbidden`). This axiom carves one narrow, opt-in exception for infrastructure noise that blocks the gate itself — not for the codebase the task is about.
Trigger: a phase or audit halts `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` with an infrastructure-shaped blocker (missing script, wrong tool version pinned in config, broken lockfile, misconfigured runner) rather than a code or design blocker.
Then, and only then, the orchestrator MAY propose a point fix scoped to environment/config artifacts only — `package.json` scripts, tool config files, lockfiles — NEVER production code under the module's `Target Files` and NEVER `specs/**` (`AX_SPEC_NEVER_EDITED` still applies to the orchestrator). The proposal is a decision-card: the blocker it resolves, the exact diff to apply, and why a narrower fix will not do. It is presented to the operator and nothing is written until the operator gives explicit approval of THAT specific diff — silence, a generic "go ahead", or approval of a different fix does not count.
Only after explicit approval: apply the diff, append ` env-fix ← ` to the Execution Log (distinct tag from `decision` / `insight`, so audit can find it without confusing it with a phase's own work), and mention the fix in `EXECUTE_SUMMARY_FORMAT`. Without approval the ticket stays `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` — the orchestrator does not apply, guess, or partially apply the fix while waiting.

SddExecuteOrchestrator.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_TASKS` | No task index / no pickable task | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK` | "next" / "pick" matches more than one pickable task — shortlist for the operator | | `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` | Unresolved blocker in the log, or a phase returned BLOCKED / FAIL — pause (NOT a failure); operator resolves, then re-runs. An infrastructure-shaped blocker MAY instead be resolved via the narrow `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` (operator-approved point fix to env/config, never code or specs) | | `H_AUDIT_FAIL_AFTER_RETRY` | Audit still FAIL after 2 attempts — manual intervention | | `H_CODE_REVIEW_BLOCKER` | Code-review returned a `BLOCKER` bug — pause for the operator (not an auto-retry) | | `H_WORKER_INTERRUPTED` | Same phase's dispatch came back with no typed Handoff twice in a row (cancelled / timed out / crashed, not a verdict) — operator checks the environment, then re-runs |
SddExecuteOrchestrator.ContextExpectation:
Everything mechanical this orchestrator needs is one of the tools below, each covered by its own tests — calling `--help` on any of them mid-run is a wasted turn against a known, stable surface; syntax here is verified against the tool's own `--help` output, kept current rather than guessed:
| Tool | When | Call | |---|---|---| | `sdd-task` (no id) | STEP_0_RESOLVE — the deterministic execution map (pickable set + blockers), computed from the trackers | `npx gennady sdd-task` | | `sdd-task ` | STEP_1_PLAN — Meta + Phases Overview + per-phase read-manifests + gates + `[BLOCKERS]`, the ONLY ticket read this directive itself does | `npx gennady sdd-task specs/app/greeting/greeting.task.APP-greet-greeting.md` | | `sdd-task --phase P` | Never called BY this directive — the worker's OWN first action (`phase-execution-protocol` STEP_1_GET_PHASE_CONTEXT). Listed here only so a `--phase` call surfacing in this directive's own trace (as at STEP_1_PLAN) is recognized as a defect, not repeated by habit | worker-only | | `sdd-task --audit-group ` | STEP_5_AUDIT — the tool's `due` / `not yet` verdict, never eyeballed | `npx gennady sdd-task --audit-group APP-greet-greeting` | | `sdd-verify --profile full` | STEP_5_AUDIT, on `due` — the mechanical pre-audit gate over the group's own working-tree diff, run BEFORE dispatching the group audit | `npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full` | | `sdd-task --group-scope ` | Resolved by the DISPATCHED audit / code-review subagent itself, its own STEP_1 — this directive never calls it directly | dispatched-subagent-only | | `sdd-log round ""` | STEP_1_PLAN — open a new Round (auto-numbered, dated) | `npx gennady sdd-log round "execute "` | | `sdd-log close` | STEP_3_CLOSE_ROUND — append the Round-close block | `npx gennady sdd-log close` | | `sdd-sync ` | STEP_4_SYNC — propagate ticket Status into every `*.3-tasks.md` from the ticket upward, verify the write | `npx gennady sdd-sync ` | | `sdd-log line "env-fix ← "` | The ONE sanctioned `line` form for this orchestrator — only after explicit operator approval of the exact diff, per `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` | `npx gennady sdd-log line "env-fix ← "` | | `sdd-state [project-root]` | Deterministic FLOW_VERSION / READINESS snapshot — STEP_0B_PREFLIGHT already gets this from the `sdd-task` map's own `гейты:` line; call directly only when nothing else has surfaced it yet | `npx gennady sdd-state` | | `sdd-check --task ` | A point re-check after a fix — never a substitute for `sdd-task`'s own lifecycle verdict at STEP_1_PLAN (that call there is the wasted-turn case the step's own text already forbids) | `npx gennady sdd-check --task ` |
`round` and `close` are this directive's ONLY two unconditional `sdd-log` modes; `phase` / `handoff` / `blocker` belong exclusively to the worker (`phase-execution-protocol`) with no exception. `line` is likewise off-limits EXCEPT the single env-fix form in the table above — the `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` write, sanctioned only after explicit prior operator approval of the exact diff; see the logging-zone rule at STEP_3_CLOSE_ROUND and `HardForbidden` below.

Step.Action:
FIRST run `sdd-task` (no Task-ID) for the deterministic execution map — the pickable set (`[ ] TODO` with every dependency `[x] DONE`, computed from the trackers) and the blocked tickets. When intent arrives as a path instead of a Task-ID, resolve the owner from the artifact (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`): a ticket path (`*.task.-.md`) carries its Task-ID in the filename; a code / spec file resolves via its `@tasks:` header (read the header, extract `@tasks: -[, ...]`, map file → [Task-IDs]; no header → ask the operator). Then route on intent:
- WHEN intent is a specific Task-ID / ticket path -> run that ticket (STEP_1–8) - WHEN intent = `next` / `pick` -> the first pickable from the map (none → H_NO_TASKS; several + ambiguous → H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK, shortlist for the operator) - WHEN intent = `batch` / `all` / `queue` -> EVERY pickable ticket in DAG order (parallel ONLY across tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint, `AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`; sequential otherwise)
The single-ticket flow (STEP_1–8) runs per selected ticket; in `batch` it loops, re-fetching the map after each ticket (statuses change as tickets finish), until the map is empty or a ticket pauses (`H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`).

Step.Goal: Clear the FLOW_VERSION/READINESS preflight gate before dispatching any phase.
Step.Action:
Use `READINESS` and `GATE_QUEUE` from the `sdd-task` map just fetched above; do not issue a second preflight call. `GATE_QUEUE` names the queued TODO tickets that build missing gates. Size the gate to this request's own blast radius (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`).
- WHEN `FLOW_VERSION=v1` AND the request's blast radius reaches the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout or task-ID rewriting -> READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/migration-v1-v2.directive.xml") (live v1→v2 migration; returns when the repo is v2) - WHEN `READINESS=not-ready` AND the already-fetched preflight input reports `GATE_QUEUE=` -> normal pre-execution state, continue your own flow; the readiness bootstrap does NOT load - WHEN `READINESS=not-ready` AND the request needs a missing gate script -> READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/readiness.directive.xml") (live setup: forces missing scripts, hands proxy-blocked installs to the operator; returns once ready) - WHEN `READINESS=provisional (stubs: …)` AND the request would run an `impl`/`refactor`/`test` phase -> STOP: those phases are mechanically refused (`ERR_CLI_SDD_TASK_INFRA_NOT_READY`) — the named stubs exit 0 verifying nothing, so any green verdict on them is a fiction. Work the infra queue first (`GATE_QUEUE`), or READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/readiness.directive.xml") when no ticket owns those stubs - WHEN `READINESS=provisional (stubs: …)` AND the request stays inside bootstrap/config/doc work, scaffold, or spec authoring -> normal pre-execution state, continue your own flow; the stub list is the infra queue's worklist, not a blocker for this request - WHEN `GATE_QUEUE_DIAG: infra-спека … одобрена, тикетов пока нет …` is printed (kind `infra-spec-no-tickets`) -> tell the operator that infra scope has no tickets yet and point at the `/sdd-scaffold` skill to cut them — a separate process, never READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE'd from here (scaffold itself hands off back into this flow, so loading it in-place would cycle) - WHEN `GATE_QUEUE_DIAG: область тикета … не совпала с порталом … (похожие имена)` is printed (kind `scope-name-mismatch`) -> fix the mismatch directly — edit the ticket's `Scope:` field or the portal scope name (whichever is the typo), never both by guesswork; not a reason to load another directive - WHEN (`FLOW_VERSION=v1` OR `READINESS=not-ready`) AND the request's blast radius stays inside its own scope (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`) -> record state in one line, continue your own flow; propose migration / readiness setup to the operator as a separate next step - DEFAULT -> repo is `v2` + `READINESS=ready` (execution-ready, no stubs) — continue your own flow

Step.Goal: Get the plan; detect state; open the Round. (one tool call, no broad ticket read)
Step.Action: `sdd-task ` returns Meta + Phases Overview + per-phase read-manifests + gates + a `[BLOCKERS]` section — the only ticket read I do. Preflight blocker scan reads that `[BLOCKERS]` section directly (`AX_BLOCKER_RESOLUTION_TRAIL`): `blockers: none` → clear to dispatch; `blockers: ACTIVE ` (each active blocker listed with its log text) → `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`. A separate `sdd-check --task` call at this step is a wasted turn — `sdd-task` already carries the same lifecycle verdict (the execute-family mirror of the router's one-`sdd-state`-call rule); `sdd-check --task` remains the tool for a point-recheck under audit, not for this step. State from Phases Overview: all `[ ]` → fresh (all phases by `Deps`); mixed → resume (remaining); all `[x]` + no audit → audit only; any `[!]` → pause. Open a new Round in the log via `sdd-log`.

Step.Goal: Dispatch workers, one phase at a time (sequential by `Deps`, `AX_EXECUTION_ORDER`).
Step.Action:
Per phase: pick the worker model by thinking-load — default by kind (`impl` / `test` → capable; `bootstrap` / `config` / `doc` → cheap), escalate to capable on LOW confidence or a reasoning-heavy phase. The worker's OWN first action is `sdd-task --phase P` (`phase-execution-protocol.directive.xml` STEP_1) — it fetches its own read-manifest, gates, and prior Handoff fresh, at the moment it starts, so the dispatch prompt itself carries NO pasted manifest. Dispatch straight from the path this directive and the resolved ticket already name — a read failure at the worker's own STEP_1 already reports a missing or broken path with an actionable message; that IS the check, so run it exactly once, where it belongs.
Session key = (this spec, this phase's kind) — per `AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE`. Look up an open worker session already keyed to this (spec, kind) pair: found AND the environment supports continuing a subagent session → send the activation below into that SAME session; not found, OR the environment cannot continue a session, OR this dispatch is a fix from an audit/code-review finding, OR this ticket's spec/group differs from the one the mapping was built for → raise a fresh worker with the SAME activation. Either path, the message is identical — dispatch it with exactly this activation:
``` Прочитай и воплоти: ai/directives/sdd-v2/phase-execution-protocol.directive.xml Задание: тикет · фаза P Первым шагом выполни: npx gennady sdd-task --phase P — и следуй его выводу. [опционально 1-3 строки контекста от оркестратора — только то, чего нет в тикете] ```
`` — то же значение, что уже разрешил STEP_0_RESOLVE/STEP_1_PLAN (Task-ID из map, либо путь): `sdd-task` резолвит голый Task-ID сам (сканирует дерево, находит тикет по Meta Task-ID), так что достаточно передать worker'у то, что уже есть под рукой — не нужен отдельный шаг резолва пути.
The optional trailing lines are the only orchestrator-authored content in the prompt — reserved for the phase kind + reason (`initial` / `fix: F-NNN` / `resume`) when it is not already inferable, and for any orchestrator knowledge genuinely absent from the ticket the tool will surface; never a restatement of read-manifest files, Rules, Target Files, or gates — the worker's own tool call already supplies those, verbatim and current. Require the report back regardless: DONE / BLOCKED / FAIL plus the worker's typed `**Handoff →**` line verbatim (`RETURN_SUMMARY_FORMAT`, `AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`) — thread exactly that into the next phase's Inputs, never a paraphrase. Emit a progress line per transition (`ORCHESTRATOR_PROGRESS_FORMAT`); the dispatch-stage line for THIS phase MUST also carry a session clause naming which path `AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE` just took — `session: reused @` when redispatched into an open session, or `session: fresh ()` when a fresh worker was raised instead — one line, always present, so a live run makes whether reuse is actually happening observable rather than assumed.
- WHEN `BLOCKED` / `FAIL` -> stop, no audit; `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR` - WHEN `DONE` -> record Handoff in working memory (for threading and the STEP_8 aggregation — the worker's own STEP_6_EMIT_HANDOFF already wrote it to the Execution Log; this directive never re-logs it), thread it into the next phase's Inputs; carry forward any `deviations:` entries verbatim (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`) — collected for STEP_8, never surfaced mid-run - WHEN the dispatch returns with no typed Handoff at all (operator-cancelled, timed out, the subagent or its environment crashed) -> this is an external interruption, not a phase verdict: not DONE, not BLOCKED, not FAIL — nobody decided anything, so log nothing as this phase's result. The work behind it may be unstarted, half-done, or fully done with the Handoff lost in transit; guessing which is unneeded. First interruption of this phase this cycle -> re-dispatch it exactly ONCE, same phase, the identical 3-line activation above — the worker's own `STEP_1B_RESUME_OR_START` finds any block it already opened for this phase and continues from there, so resuming never redoes or duplicates logged work. Same phase interrupted again on that retry -> stop, no audit; `H_WORKER_INTERRUPTED`

Append Round close via `sdd-log` (`ROUND_CLOSE_FORMAT`); set Meta Status `[x] DONE`. The ticket log outlives this dispatch — audit and any future session read only the file, with no memory of this run, so the close line and every threaded Handoff must already carry everything they need (`AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT`). **Logging-zone boundary:** `round` (STEP_1_PLAN) and `close` (here) are this directive's ONLY two Execution Log writes for the whole cycle. Every phase header, event line, and Handoff line already exists in the log — the worker wrote each one itself via its own `sdd-log phase` / `line` / `handoff` calls (`phase-execution-protocol` STEP_1B_RESUME_OR_START / STEP_6_EMIT_HANDOFF, `AX_TICKET_WRITE_SCOPE`) before returning DONE. Re-logging a phase heading or a Handoff line from here duplicates the worker's own entry — exactly the class of finding a prior audit round caught — never a safety net.
`sdd-sync ` updates the scope + project trackers and verifies the write (`AX_VERIFY_AND_FINALIZE`).

Step.Goal: Ask the tool whether this ticket's group is due for review; dispatch only when it is (`AX_AUDIT_HOOK`).
Step.Action:
Run `sdd-task --audit-group ` — the tool decides the moment, never eyeballed. It prints the owning spec, the group's full ticket list with statuses, and the verdict.
- WHEN `not yet` (the tool names tickets still open) -> dispatch NEITHER audit nor code-review this cycle; this ticket's own phase gates and tests already closed it (Meta Status `[x] DONE` stands) — skip straight to STEP_8_SUMMARY for this ticket's cycle, then the next pickable ticket in the queue. A ticket's own dependents INSIDE this same group already unblocked on ITS closure, independent of the group's audit state. - WHEN `due` (every ticket in the group is `[x] DONE`) -> BEFORE dispatching the audit, run `npx gennady sdd-verify --profile full` over the group: mechanical cleanliness precedes semantic review. `yagni` diffs against HEAD, and this execute flow never commits mid-run — by the time a group closes, the working tree still carries the diff of the WHOLE spec's changes, exactly the base `yagni` needs; this is deliberate, not a gap to "optimize" by inserting an interim commit. RED -> dispatch the fix through the ordinary fix-flow (fresh worker session per `AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE`); a `yagni` finding specifically routes to a waiver decision per `AX_USAGE_WAIVER_DISCIPLINE`, logged into the ticket that owns the flagged entity. Re-run `sdd-verify --profile full` until GREEN — EXCEPT one verdict no worker can fix: `⛔ обязательная ступень профиля` (the project's own verification scripts are missing or stubbed). That is infrastructure, not code: no fix-flow dispatch can turn it green, so looping on it never terminates. Surface it to the operator instead — name the missing/stubbed scripts and the infra tickets that own them (`sdd-task` → `GATE_QUEUE`), leave the group open, and stop; the audit does not dispatch on an unverified group. Only THEN dispatch ONE audit-subagent on a cheap model (audit is mechanical verification): read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/audit.directive.xml`; group = the id `sdd-task --audit-group` just confirmed `due`; mode per-group. Its own STEP_1 resolves the full scope itself (`sdd-task --group-scope `) — this dispatch prompt carries no pasted manifest or artifact list, same self-bootstrap pattern as phase dispatch. Wait for the verdict.

Step.Goal: Branch on the group audit verdict.

Action.LogicSwitch: - WHEN `PASS` / `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` -> STEP_7B_CODE_REVIEW (a `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` here always already carries a Decision Log entry — audit only confirms a PRIOR acceptance, per `audit.directive`; it never asks live) - WHEN `FAIL` + attempt 1 + every open finding carries a concrete mechanical remediation the orchestrator can apply (via Path B — ticket / Decision Log / waiver-label edits — or via `phases_to_fix` → apply/re-run per STEP_7_RESOLVE, whichever the finding calls for) -> STEP_7_RESOLVE, apply every finding's fix directly (no operator stop — a finding with a concrete mechanical fix is not a risk decision), then re-dispatch audit (R2); a `phases_to_fix` re-run ALWAYS raises a fresh worker session, never the session that ran the original phase (`AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE` — fresh eyes on a fix, no exception) - WHEN `FAIL` + only open `MAJOR` findings (no open `BLOCKER`) + attempt 1 + at least one open finding has NO concrete mechanical remediation (it can only be accepted as-is — an open gate-risk, an environment limitation) -> ask the operator, per such finding: accept this risk? ALL accepted -> STEP_7_RESOLVE Path B (append a Decision Log entry per accepted finding — the acceptance record the next audit dispatch will find — no new Round), then re-dispatch audit (R2, which now returns `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS`); ANY declined -> STEP_7_RESOLVE as an ordinary `FAIL` (Path A/B per the finding's fix, not an acceptance) - WHEN `FAIL` (open `BLOCKER`, or a declined risk) + attempt 1 -> STEP_7_RESOLVE (one retry) - WHEN `FAIL` + attempt 2 -> H_AUDIT_FAIL_AFTER_RETRY, then STEP_8 (`AX_RE_DISPATCH` caps at 2)

Step.Goal: Resolve audit findings (one retry) — the real fix, not the deferring shortcut.
Step.Action: Resolve findings at release-ready depth (`AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT`): re-running a phase to actually fix error handling / an edge case a finding surfaced is Path A, never a Path B label that defers it without an operator decision and a Decision Log risk entry. Path A — `phases_to_fix` non-empty: a group audit's findings may name phases on ANY ticket in the group, not only the ticket whose closure triggered this dispatch — open a new Round on each phase's OWNING ticket; re-run ONLY those phases as `fix` (sequential, per owning ticket) in a FRESH worker session per phase, never the (spec, kind) session that ran the phase originally (`AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE` — the agent that wrote the bug is the wrong one to re-look at it), then STEP_3 → STEP_5 (re-check `sdd-task --audit-group`, audit R2). Path B — findings are ticket / spec / decision-log only (administrative artifact edits: tracker fields, Decision Log entries, a contract Usage Waiver label in the spec — never production code): apply them directly under the orchestrator's own artifact-edit channel (the orchestrator owns trackers and may make these administrative edits, `AX_OWNER`; distinct from and narrower than `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL`, which covers env/config, not artifacts — see `HardForbidden`), no new Round, then re-dispatch audit (R2). Either way return to STEP_6. An R2 verdict that skipped a full gate re-run is invalid — before accepting R2's verdict at STEP_6, the orchestrator MUST confirm the R2 summary carries every gate line (`sdd-check --task`, `sdd-check --changed`, `sdd-verify --profile full`, `gennady lint --spec`, `gennady testcov`), and if any is missing, return the audit dispatch for rework rather than act on it.

Step.Goal: Dispatch fresh-eyes code-review for the group (lazy, same trigger as audit — right after it passes).
Step.Action: Dispatch ONE code-review subagent (isolated): read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/code-review.directive.xml`; group = the same id the group audit just covered; mode per-group. Its own STEP_1 resolves the full scope itself (`sdd-task --group-scope `) — no pasted manifest or artifact list in this dispatch prompt, same self-bootstrap pattern as the audit dispatch above. It scopes to bugs only (correctness / edge / error-path / security), leaving drift and style out. Verdict: `CLEAN` → STEP_8; `FINDINGS` with a `BLOCKER` → `H_CODE_REVIEW_BLOCKER` (pause for the operator); `FINDINGS` non-blocking → carry into the summary as routed proposals, STEP_8.

Step.Goal: Summarize for the operator; report every self-resolved deviation from the whole cycle in one batch.
Step.Action: Aggregate phase + audit telemetry; present per `EXECUTE_SUMMARY_FORMAT`. When this ticket's cycle hit `not yet` at STEP_5 (its group is not fully closed), the summary carries no audit / code-review verdict for this cycle — state plainly that review is deferred to the group's close, per `AX_AUDIT_HOOK`, rather than omitting the line silently — the group's per-kind worker sessions stay open in this case, since the group itself has not closed yet. Once the group DOES close this cycle (audit + code-review both ran), every worker session keyed to it closes together with the group (`AX_WORKER_SESSION_REUSE`) — the next spec/group starts with fresh sessions, never carrying this group's context forward. Collect every worker Handoff `deviations:` entry across the ENTIRE cycle just run — one ticket's Round, or every Round of a `batch` loop — plus any spec/ticket gap the orchestrator itself self-resolved directly at STEP_1 / STEP_2 / STEP_6 rather than delegating to a worker (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`). Empty set → nothing to ask, summary stands alone. Non-empty → ONE batched `AskUserQuestion` (`QUESTION_RULE_SLIM`) right after the summary, covering every deviation together — never one question per deviation, never mid-run: per deviation, «внести в спеку» / «откатить» / «принять как есть». This is the only point deviations reach the operator; the legal live pauses (`H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`, `H_CODE_REVIEW_BLOCKER`, the STEP_6 risk-accept dialogue) are a separate class — environment/risk, not a spec hole — and keep firing live exactly as today.

SddExecuteOrchestrator.HardForbidden: - Workers read phase bodies / BDD / Verification / specs / rule files / code, each bounded by their manifest; the orchestrator does not. - Workers write code, audit reports, and phase blocks; the orchestrator does not write production code, ever. It has exactly THREE narrow, non-overlapping write channels: (a) `AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL` — env/config artifacts only (`package.json` scripts, tool config, lockfiles), never `Target Files` code or `specs/**`, never without prior explicit operator approval of the exact diff; (b) STEP_7_RESOLVE Path B — administrative edits to ticket / Decision Log / spec waiver-labels, applying an ACCEPTED audit finding directly per `AX_OWNER`; (c) a ticket-local Decision Log append when the orchestrator itself self-resolves a spec/ticket hole it hit directly, not delegated to a worker (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`) — distinct from (b), which is gated on an audit finding the operator already accepted, while (c) fires on a gap the orchestrator decides on its own and reports only in the STEP_8 batch. None of the three extends to production code under a module's `Target Files`. - Run the group audit only when `sdd-task --audit-group` reports the group `due` — never per ticket, never on eyeballed "this looks like the last one"; run code-review immediately after that audit passes, on the same trigger, never independently of it. - Thread only typed Handoff payloads between subagents; keep their contexts separate. - This directive's own `sdd-log` calls are `round` (STEP_1_PLAN) and `close` (STEP_3_CLOSE_ROUND), unconditionally — `phase` / `handoff` / `blocker` are forbidden with no exception, the worker's exclusive writes (`phase-execution-protocol`, `AX_TICKET_WRITE_SCOPE`); this directive never re-logs a phase header or a Handoff line the worker already wrote. `line` is forbidden EXCEPT the single sanctioned form `sdd-log line "env-fix ← "`, and only after explicit operator approval of the exact diff (`AX_ENV_FIX_CHANNEL`) — every other `line` call remains off-limits. - Cap audit attempts at 2; re-run only phases in `phases_to_fix`; drive a retry from audit FAIL only (a phase BLOCKED pauses, it does not reopen); run phases of the same task sequentially, one at a time.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
A question to the operator fires only through `AskUserQuestion` — or, when the tool is unavailable, a plain-text fallback carrying the same context plus an explicit list of named options — and always after the context is explained in the same message, never as bare free-form text. Batch mutually independent sub-questions into one call; dependent questions go one call at a time, composed only after the previous answer is in. No numbering, no semantic question IDs.
Full format, with worked examples — `QUESTION_FORMAT` in the interview / vision directives.

ChatOutput.Contract:
Subagents are black boxes; emit one progress line per state transition so the operator sees the run. `[] % | | ` Stages: `⏳ resolving + planning` · `🔧 phase

(, ) executing` · `✅ phase

done → next` · `✅ all phases done → 🔍 audit` · `✅ audit PASS`. Retry path: `❌ audit FAIL → 🔄 re-run as fix` · `✅ re-run done → 🔍 audit R2`. Pause path (NOT a failure — awaiting the operator): `✋ PAUSED — `; the operator marks resolution in the Execution Log, then re-runs.

Final operator summary once audit settles. Plain, scannable:
📊 Task `` — Execute + Audit 🔧 Round 1: `P1 (impl, sonnet) ✅` · `P2 (test, haiku) ✅` · … 🔍 Round 1 audit: `✅ PASS` | `❌ FAIL (🔴 N · 🟠 M)` 🔄 Round 2 (if any): `P2 (fix) ✅` · audit R2 `✅` 📊 Final: `✅ PASS` | `⚠️ PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` | `❌ FAIL` ⏱️ wall total · 📍 files touched · ⚠️ problems encountered
If the run self-resolved any spec/ticket hole (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`), one more line before the batched `AskUserQuestion`: 🧭 Deviations: `-D-N — ` · `-D-M — ` · … No deviations → omit the line entirely, no batched question fires.
